evidence: Cic. Off. 1.18: ad cognitiōnis et scientiae cupiditātem
Caes. BG 3.8.1: scientiā atque ūsū rērum nauticārum
terms.comment: What one knows goes in the genitive (scientia rērum nauticārum). Set against ūsus, practice, it is knowledge in theory (Cic. Rep. 1.2; see theory).

terms.gloss: learning, what one has been taught
evidence: Cic. Fam. 6.12.5: est ūnum perfugium doctrīna ac litterae

phrases.latin: Omnēs enim trahimur et dūcimur ad cognitiōnis et scientiae cupiditātem, in quā excellere pulchrum putāmus
phrases.english: for we are all drawn and led to the desire for learning and knowledge, and we think it a fine thing to excel in it

phrases.latin: sed est ūnum perfugium doctrīna ac litterae, quibus semper ūsī sumus
phrases.english: but there is one refuge, learning and books, which we have always made use of

sources: Lewis & Short: scientia · Lewis & Short: cognitio · Lewis & Short: doctrina
